newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Hondurans seek expulsion of U.S. labor activist.
newsitem.headline: Hondurans seek expulsion of U.S. labor activist.

text.p: Honduran business leaders on Thursday asked the government to expel a U.S. labour activist who has denounced alleged sweatshop-style labour abuses in this Central American country.

The Honduran Council of Private Enterprise (COHEP) is targeting Charles Kernaghan, a leader of the U.S. National Labour Committee, who has protested against labour conditions for textile workers in Honduras.

COHEP, the most powerful business group in Honduras, accuses Kernaghan of damaging the country's image abroad and says he could put thousands of people out of work if Honduran clothing exports are affected.

"We have to declare him persona non grata and bring an energetic protest before the U.S. government to show what kind of problem these people are causing," Juan Bendeck, president of COHEP, told reporters.
"Nobody has really put him in his place," Bendeck said. "I think we have to set a precedent because we could all of a sudden have thousands of unemployed people in the street because of his fault."

Kernaghan's group has presented at least two underaged Honduran textile workers before U.S. lawmakers as examples of abuse in the "maquiladora" industry here. Kernaghan, who is believed to be out of Honduras at the moment, has told reporters he does not oppose the industry but seeks better working conditions for employees.

Controversy has brewed in Washington in the past year over alleged Central American sweatshops, with activists charging that cheap labour is abused in making clothing destined for the U.S. market. More than 75,000 workers are employed by an industry that exports $1.2 billion worth of goods a year.
